== Biography ==

'''John de Glasgu I''' is securely documented in two Glasgow civic property acts dated 1447 and 1455. These records form a concrete person-level bridge across 1450: the same name appears in the same burgh, in the same class of property proceeding, within the same civic and notarial network.

The identification of the two appearances as one man is assessed at '''very high confidence'''. Both instruments were drawn up by Henry Michael, notary and clerk of Glasgow's burgh court; both concern property close to Glasgow Cross; and the printed volume's index groups the entries under ''Johannes de Glasgu''.

The 1447 wording places John within a group expressly described as '''burgesses of Glasgow'''. A working birth estimate is '''before c.1425–30''', based on his burgess status by 1447.

Malcolm is the strongest preceding-generation candidate because he was explicitly a son of a Glasgow-designated father and was active early enough to father the burgess; no record names Malcolm's own children.

He should be kept separate from '''John Glasgw of Stirling''', documented in 1475 and 1479/80, and from '''John of Glasgow alias Smith''', documented in 1506. A generational relationship remains possible, but no parentage, succession, shared property, seal or repeated associate proves one.

=== 1. Glasgow burgess and civic witness, 1447–1455 ===

==== 21 June 1447: Walkergate ====

On 21 June 1447 Alexander Sawar, burgess of Glasgow, sold an annual rent of 3s 6d from a rood or parcel of land on the west side of the '''Walkergate'''. The property lay between the land of John Ade on the north and that of William Stevenson on the south.

The witnesses included Thomas Wyntir, bailie, followed by John Red, John Ade, '''John de Glasgu''', William Oglach, William Stevenson and William Jackson, with Robert Pettigrew, sergeant, and others.<ref name="John1447">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine: Munimenta Fratrum Predicatorum de Glasgu'' (Glasgow, 1846), act dated 21 June 1447; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

The crucial Latin places the named lay witnesses within the collective description ''burgensibus''. Thomas Wyntir is separately identified as bailie and Robert Pettigrew as sergeant. The natural grammatical reading is that John Red, John Ade, '''John de Glasgu''', William Oglach, William Stevenson and William Jackson were burgesses.

Accordingly:

* '''John de Glasgu was a burgess of Glasgow by 21 June 1447''';
* he appeared as a formal witness to a sale and delivery of sasine;
* he had no stated ownership or financial interest in the property;
* and no occupation, office or family relationship is supplied.

The '''Walkergate''', also written Waulkersgait or Walcargate, was the street of the cloth-fullers. It corresponds to modern '''Saltmarket''', running south from Glasgow Cross towards the medieval South Port and the Clyde.

==== Name form and surname-like use ====

The 1447 wording distinguishes between:

* ''Alexander Sawar burgensis de Glasgu'' — Alexander Sawar, burgess of Glasgow; and
* ''Johanne de Glasgu'' — John de Glasgu.

The same distinction recurs in 1455, where John Stenson is described as a burgess of Glasgow but the witness is simply John de Glasgu.

This suggests that ''de Glasgu'' was functioning as John's stable personal byname or surname-like identifier rather than merely stating residence. Its use inside Glasgow itself strengthens that interpretation.

The evidence does not prove hereditary transmission. No securely identified father, son, brother or other relative is known to use the same designation.

==== 10 April 1455: Fullers' Street and St Thenew's Street ====

The published Latin dates the second act to '''10 April 1455'''. A modern archival catalogue appears to date the corresponding item to '''19 April 1455'''; the original parchment should be checked to resolve the discrepancy.

John Stenson, burgess of Glasgow, sold Master David de Cadyoche, precentor of Glasgow Cathedral, an annual rent of 3s from a tenement on the west side of the '''Vicus Fullonum'''. Mariota Dwn, widow of the late William de Kerswell, also sold him an annual rent of 2s from a tenement on the north side of the '''Vicus Beate Tenaw'''.

The witnesses included John Macmulan, bailie, David Hyne, Andrew Brady, '''John de Glasgu''' and Robert Fausyde, sergeant, with others.<ref name="John1455">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 10 April 1455 in the published Latin; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

John again appears in a formal civic witness group containing a bailie and the burgh sergeant. He had no stated financial or proprietary interest in either annual rent.

''Vicus Fullonum'' means Street of the Fullers and is the Latin equivalent of Walkergate, now Saltmarket. ''Vicus Beate Tenaw'' was St Thenew's Street, corresponding broadly to modern Trongate.

The two records therefore place John repeatedly in civic property business close to Glasgow Cross. There is no substantial reason to treat them as different men.

=== 2. Legal and civic setting ===

Both instruments were drawn up by '''Henry Michael''', clerk of the Diocese of Glasgow and notary public.

A separate instrument dated 10 May 1454 describes Henry Michael as ''scriba curie Glasguensis et notario'' — clerk or scribe of the Glasgow court and notary.<ref name="HenryMichael">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 10 May 1454, describing Henry Michael as clerk of the Glasgow court and notary; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

John's two appearances therefore belong to the same professional burgh legal network. This supports his accepted standing within Glasgow's burgess community, but does not prove that he was literate, legally trained, a notary, merchant, craftsman or civic officer.

==== Walkergate witness network ====

A separate act dated 9 September 1454 describes a Walkergate property bounded by the tenement of '''John Reid''' on the north and '''William Oglach''' on the south.<ref name="WalkergateNetwork">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 9 September 1454; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

William Oglach is an exact match to John's 1447 fellow witness. John Red and John Reid are probably the same person, though that identification remains qualified. At least part of the witness group was therefore drawn from burgesses with property interests in the immediate neighbourhood. John's own residence or ownership there is not proved.

==== Brady–Brade–Spreull network context ====

The 1455 witness list places '''Andrew Brady''' alongside John de Glasgu. This does not prove kinship, but it is relevant to the later civic network.

A Glasgow property description of 1430 referred to land of the '''heirs of Walter Sprewl'''.<ref name="Spreull1430">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', Glasgow property act of 1430 describing land of the heirs of Walter Sprewl; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

On 27 November 1488 William Sprwl and his wife Joneta Burl sold an annual rent from a Glasgow tenement, witnessed by '''Robert Brade'''.<ref name="BradeSpreull1488">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 27 November 1488, recording William Sprwl and Joneta Burl and naming Robert Brade as witness; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

On 31 December 1534 William Glasgow and Esbell Brade transferred property to their son John Glasgow and his wife Jonet Spreull.<ref name="WilliamBradeSpreull1534">''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', protocol dated 31 December 1534, recording William Glasgow and Esbell Brade, their son John Glasgow and his wife Jonet Spreull.</ref>

The sequence creates a '''civic and property-network bridge''' into the milieu of the first proved sixteenth-century pedigree. It is not a pedigree. No inspected record proves that Andrew Brady was related to Robert or Esbell Brade, or that the earlier Spreulls were ancestors of Jonet Spreull.

=== 3. Relationship to the other Johns ===

A separate '''John Glasgw''' witnessed Stirling acts in 1475 and 1479/80. He may have been the same man, a son, a nephew or an unrelated bearer. Splitting the profiles is the safer treatment because no direct bridge identifies them.

John de Glasgu I should not be merged with John alias Smith or the Saltmarket property-holder. Extending the 1447 burgess to the Saltmarket record of 1548 would require an implausibly long adult career.

=== 4. Surviving originals and archival leads ===

The printed ''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'' states that the instruments were abbreviated from original documents preserved among the University of Glasgow's Blackhouse Charters.

|-
! Act !! Catalogue item !! Suggested archive reference
|-
| 21 June 1447 || Blackhouse item 0068 || GUA 12418
|-
| April 1455 || Blackhouse item 0082 || GUA 12430

These identifications should be checked directly with Glasgow University Archives.<ref name="BlackhouseArchive">University of Glasgow Archives & Special Collections, Blackhouse Charters information and catalogue access; [https://www.gla.ac.uk/myglasgow/archivespecialcollections/discover/university/features/blackhouse/ University of Glasgow].</ref>

Images could establish the precise spelling and abbreviation of John's name, whether ''burgensibus'' unquestionably encompasses him, the full witness order, the correct April 1455 date, and any omitted status or occupation.

=== Evidence assessment ===

The secure evidence establishes that:

* John de Glasgu was a burgess of Glasgow by 1447;
* he witnessed Glasgow property acts in 1447 and 1455;
* the two acts concern the same individual at very high confidence;
* both were recorded by Henry Michael;
* both involved property close to Glasgow Cross;
* and the records provide a concrete person-level bridge across 1450.

The evidence does not establish his occupation, property ownership, wife, children, parentage, relationship to the Stirling John, or descent to the later Glasgow families.

=== Timeline summary ===

* '''before c.1425–30''' — working birth estimate based on burgess status by 1447
* '''21 June 1447''' — witnesses a west-side Walkergate transaction as a Glasgow burgess
* '''10 April 1455''' — witnesses Fullers' Street and St Thenew's Street transactions; Andrew Brady appears in the same group

'''Secure records assigned to John de Glasgu I:''' 2.

== For further research ==

* Obtain images of GUA 12418 and GUA 12430.
* Resolve the 10 April / 19 April 1455 date discrepancy.
* Compare the full witness networks in the two instruments.
* Reconstruct Andrew Brady's family without prematurely normalising Brady and Brade as one surname.
* Search for explicit relationship or succession terms linking John to the Stirling and sixteenth-century bearers.
